message: The unquoted heredoc preserves the backslashes in `command -v \\"${binary}\\"`. Consequently, the generated probe executes `command -v \\"jq\\"`, looking for a binary whose name includes literal double-quote characters rather than `jq`. Since jq is the first non-wrapper manifest entry, even a correctly provisioned deployment fails Check 3 with `missing_binary:jq`, before reaching the direct-exec gemini check. Sandbox image verification uses the same broken probe. Remove the backslashes before the argument's double quotes, retaining the escaped dollar sign for deferred command substitution. Evidence: scripts/verify.sh@ac6e2196f5c307fd09fa6ad8a64ba9ada14ab385:277-300 and scripts/docker/runtime-binaries.json@ac6e2196f5c307fd09fa6ad8a64ba9ada14ab385:1-11.

The unquoted heredoc preserves the backslashes in `command -v \\"${binary}\\"`: backslash-double-quote is not an escape processed during heredoc expansion. The generated shell probe therefore searches for a filename containing literal quote characters, such as `"jq"`, rather than `jq`. Since jq is the first manifest entry on both architectures, healthy deployments fail Check 3 with `missing_binary:jq` before reaching the Gemini direct-exec check; sandbox verification uses the same broken probe. Remove the backslashes around `${binary}` in the heredoc. Evidence: scripts/verify.sh@ac6e2196f5c307fd09fa6ad8a64ba9ada14ab385:277-301 and scripts/docker/runtime-binaries.json@ac6e2196f5c307fd09fa6ad8a64ba9ada14ab385:1-11.

The new validation bounds pattern length but does not guard against catastrophic backtracking. For example, `^(a+)+$` with flag `g` passes validation, and executing it against `'a'.repeat(40) + '!'` also passes the inline-code limit. The engine then calls native `regex.exec` synchronously without a time budget, allowing exponential backtracking to block the event loop and make the MCP server unresponsive. The claimed ReDoS protection needs a linear-time regex engine, unsafe-pattern rejection, or isolated execution with an enforceable timeout.

The new path-size guard trusts `stats.size`, but the handler accepts special files and subsequently performs an unbounded `fs.promises.readFile` through `src/utils/fileUtils.ts` (HEAD lines 51–52). On Unix, `{ "path": "/dev/zero" }` passes the existence check and reports a size of zero, then continuously supplies bytes to the read until resource exhaustion or read failure. Thus the 500,000-byte cap can be bypassed even when no custom rules are installed. Reject non-regular files and bound the actual read to the limit plus one byte; a bounded read also protects against files growing between `stat` and `readFile`.

The new limits do not prevent catastrophic backtracking. For example, a rule using `^(a+)+$` passes validation, and inline code containing a few dozen `a` characters followed by `!` is well below the input cap. At HEAD 16a54f0f85a9091f220418850eac6b4122782be5, this accepted regex executes synchronously through `matchLineIssues` (src/core/customRulesEngine.ts:153-156,184), reached by the MCP handler (src/server/handlers.ts:425-460). Matching can therefore block the server's event loop for an exponentially long time despite all new guards. Use complexity-safe matching or execute regexes in a terminable worker with a deadline.

The security-hardened execution path still hangs indefinitely for an accepted Unicode regex: use pattern `(?:)`, flags `gu`, and code `😀`. At HEAD 16a54f0f85a9091f220418850eac6b4122782be5, validation accepts this short pattern and flag combination (src/core/customRulesEngine.ts:253-275). After an empty match at index 0, `lastIndex++` moves into the surrogate pair; Unicode-aware `exec` backs up to its beginning and returns the same empty match again. This repeats forever, blocking the MCP server even with a two-code-unit input. Advance by a complete Unicode code point when `regex.unicode` is true.

Both authentication tabs list only ExternalConnection.ReadWrite.OwnedBy, which is insufficient for the content-ingestion check. At head revision a44ec57153539d3b87c3d8fe819575574b2dee9e, src/m365/external/commands/connection/connection-doctor.ts:388-466 searches externalItem entities through /v1.0/search/query and then retrieves an external item. These operations require external-item access; include ExternalItem.Read.All in the documented permissions. Users granting only the listed permission can load the connection and schema but receive an authorization failure for the content-ingestion check, causing a correctly configured connection to be reported as failing that check.

An existing fallback installation is never updated or removed once a supported tool is detected. For example, install skills with no tool signals, then add `.cursor/` and upgrade to a CLI with newer skill versions: `init` updates only `.cursor/skills/`, leaving the old `.agents/skills/` intact. Meanwhile, `checkStaleness` explicitly includes existing `.agents/` installations (packages/cli/src/install/install.ts at head d7b6f3f5d8ce72d2922533e578585a5ce422bc95, lines 300–307), so `info` continues reporting outdated Agent Skills even after reinitialization. Handle the previous fallback installation when transitioning to detected tools, either by refreshing it or cleaning up its Taskless-owned skills.

An existing fallback installation stops receiving updates once any supported tool is detected. For example, install into .agents/skills/, subsequently add CLAUDE.md or .cursor/, and run init with newer embedded skills: only the detected tool's installation is refreshed, leaving the universal installation at its old version. checkStaleness explicitly includes an existing .agents directory even alongside detected tools (packages/cli/src/install/install.ts at head d7b6f3f5d8ce72d2922533e578585a5ce422bc95, lines 296–306), so info can continue reporting outdated Agent Skills immediately after a successful init, and rerunning init cannot repair them. Update an already-existing fallback installation alongside detected tools, or remove obsolete Taskless-owned fallback skills during the transition.

Pagination is sent in the URL query string instead of the JSON GET request body required by the public issue. The same defect occurs in listRecipientSubscribers() (lines 1918–1926) and listRecipientTags() (lines 1942–1950). At head revision 778a137bbaa1aa3ecc25970da48655620bab8632, all three methods omit the body entirely, so a body-based endpoint cannot receive the requested page or page size and can repeatedly return its default page, preventing callers from enumerating recipients. The new tests assert query parameters and an undefined body rather than checking the required serialization. Implement the documented body-based pagination using a transport capable of sending GET bodies.

Pagination is sent as URL query parameters rather than the JSON GET request body required by the public issue's API contract. The same defect occurs in listRecipientSubscribers() (lines 1917–1925) and listRecipientTags() (lines 1941–1948). Against the described body-based API, calls requesting later pages or a custom page size provide no pagination payload, leaving pagination at server defaults and potentially causing page iteration to repeatedly retrieve the first page. The new tests only assert the query-string behavior using a mocked fetch; they do not establish that the server supports it. Implement the documented pagination transport with a compatible transport, or verify that the API accepts query parameters.

Attachment export is described as optional, but bacula-log-archiver.gs at head revision bc9e7308ec630018a9402979ff6432965e238398, lines 49–52, unconditionally saves every message attachment to Drive. Neither the script nor the documented setup provides an opt-out. Users following this documentation for PDF-only audit collection will also copy attachments into the destination folder. Describe attachment export as automatic when attachments are present, or implement and document an explicit option to disable it.

Reusing the Statistics object does not preserve a consistent snapshot. StatisticsLoaderThread passes the DataManager's Note objects into Statistics without copying them, while MonthChart recalculates daily counts from those objects whenever the dialog is constructed or its filters change. If a retained note is edited between visits, the monthly heatmap reflects its changed text while the cached overview totals, yearly/weekly counts and phrases remain unchanged. Snapshot the note data or cache the daily aggregates as well so all tabs represent the same statistics until refresh.

A cancellation callback clears the shared cache and loading flag without checking whether its loader is still active. StatisticsLoaderThread can emit cancellation twice: chunkComplete() emits it when the user cancels, but run() continues waiting for the worker futures and emits it again if a remaining worker subsequently fails. If the user starts a replacement load between those events, the obsolete callback marks that replacement idle or erases its completed cache, permitting overlapping loads and out-of-order publication. Associate callbacks with an active loader or generation and ignore obsolete callbacks.

Reusing this Statistics object does not preserve a consistent snapshot across tabs. StatisticsLoaderThread.getStatistics() passes dataManager.getNotes() into Statistics, which retains the list without copying its mutable Note objects (HEAD StatisticsLoaderThread.java:72-86 and Statistics.java:35-49). The Months chart queries those notes and recounts their current text each time it is constructed (HEAD charts/MonthChart.java:132-146), whereas the overview, year/week totals and phrases remain precomputed. If a retained Note is edited between dialog visits, reopening the dialog can therefore show updated word counts in Months alongside old totals elsewhere, even though no refresh was requested. Snapshot the note data used by Months, or cache its daily aggregates together with the other statistics. All cited HEAD spans are at revision 8ef352bd1d5402b18b076bad6af7a34c96940e6a.
